definition: A people counter is an electronic device that is used to measure the number of people traversing a certain passage or entrance.
details: Examples include simple manual clickers, smart-flooring technologies, infrared beams, thermal imaging systems, Wi-Fi trackers and video counters using advanced machine learning algorithms. They are commonly used by retail establishments to judge the effectiveness of marketing campaigns, building design and layout, and the popularity of particular brands.

explainer.lead: An electronic device that measures the number of people crossing a passage or entrance. Retailers use it to judge marketing effectiveness, building layout and brand popularity.

tiers.eli5: It is a sensor at a doorway that keeps a tally of how many people walk through.
tiers.practitioner: Choices range from manual clickers and infrared beams to thermal imaging, Wi-Fi tracking and video counters using machine learning. A pitfall is that counts can be off when people pass side by side or linger in the sensing zone.
tiers.paperLevel: A people counter measures the number of people traversing a given passage or entrance; implementations include manual clickers, smart flooring, infrared beams, thermal imaging, Wi-Fi trackers and ML-based video counters.

explainer.example: A shop installs a video counter at its entrance using machine learning to detect each person crossing the threshold, tallying daily footfall to compare against sales.
